A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TINN research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison; the original appendices can be matched to their expanded and renumbered counterparts.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural PDE-solving experiments, including five benchmark comparisons in Table 2, architectural and optimizer ablations, and derivative-error and training-stability analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds further PDE and inverse-problem results, a parameter-trajectory diagnostic, and additional controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: The core time embedding, affine parameter lift, physics-informed objective and LM algorithm remain unchanged. Limited procedural extensions include learning two unknown Burgers coefficients in Appendix B.10 and using ten time windows for Kuramoto–Sivashinsky in Appendix B.6.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original five forward PDE benchmarks and adds Kuramoto–Sivashinsky, two-dimensional flow mixing, three-dimensional Klein–Gordon and Navier–Stokes, inverse Burgers coefficient identification, and a transport-equation comparison. Appendices B.6–B.10 and E.1 substantially broaden the dynamics, dimensionality and task requirements evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated HyperPINN-style comparator (Table 6), direct SPINN comparison (Table 7), and the previously only discussed space–time separation method (Section 2.2 and Appendix E.1). Compact PirateNet also joins the LM ablation in Tables 4 and 16, although larger PirateNet models already appeared elsewhere in v1.

E3.justification: The original main-experiment configurations, sampling counts and metrics are retained. New protocols include a common Adam learning-rate schedule across architectures, compact PirateNet under LM, controlled single/double-precision trials, small-model optimizer comparisons, and iteration/time-to-target-error measurements. New tasks additionally introduce ten-window training and inverse identification from 2,000 observations.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a KdV singular-value diagnostic testing whether fitted parameter trajectories are approximately rank one. Expanded architectural controls and Appendices E.2–E.6 examine compact versus full hypernetwork modulation, architecture versus training strategy, precision effects, convergence efficiency and optimizer dependence, substantially extending v1's ablations.

E5.justification: Five-seed experiments and mean/standard-deviation reporting already appear in v1 and are retained. V2 newly specifies that the previously claimed 10.55× and 2.30× speedups use seed 4 (Table 14). This qualifies their statistical scope; it does not establish increased replication or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 and retained ablation entries are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results, including errors of 5.20E-05 for three-dimensional Klein–Gordon and 4.05E-04 for Navier–Stokes. New comparisons also show HyperPINN slightly outperforming TINN on Allen–Cahn (Table 6) and MLP outperforming TINN on Klein–Gordon under the common Adam protocol (Table 7). These are additional findings under new comparisons, not revised main-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds spatial and mixed-derivative bounds for shallow networks with bounded activation derivatives, contrasting fixed and time-varying derivative envelopes. Appendix A.2 adds an affine-trajectory dimensionality argument. These extend the mathematical explanation, while Proposition 5.1 and the LM derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its optimizer contribution from developing an LM-based optimizer to employing one, and incorporates identifying time entanglement into the architectural contribution. The central TINN claim and abstract's approximately 4× error improvement and 10× convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets nearly rank-one parameter trajectories as support for compact temporal embeddings and argues from the precision controls that gains are not primarily precision artifacts. It also discusses stronger optimizers benefiting small TINNs and accumulated integration error in the separation method. These refine the existing mechanism explanation without replacing it.

D1.justification: V2 supplies model structures, iteration budgets or observation counts for added tasks and compact-PirateNet LM settings in Table 16; the original configuration tables are retained. It changes the listed repository owner from CYDai-nycu to CYDai-ml and adds a supplementary-code reproducibility statement. Actual code availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds HyperPINN, PINN failure-mode and loss-landscape studies, and RoPINN, clarifying differences from full hypernetworks and compatibility with training improvements. These are focused positioning additions. Datar et al.'s change from a 2024 preprint to a 2026 publication refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain. Changes include localized contribution and related-work revisions, widespread replacement of 'accuracy' with more explicit error terminology, updated publication information and cross-references, and new impact/reproducibility statements. Appendices are expanded and renumbered rather than comprehensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds solution/prediction/error panels for Kuramoto–Sivashinsky and flow mixing (Figures 7–8), diagnostic and comparison Tables 5–10 and 14, and PirateNet rows in the LM ablation displays. Figures 1–6 retain their original graphics, while existing tables are relocated or renumbered. The added visual evidence substantially expands the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for the architectural contribution through the HyperPINN comparison, additional architecture controls, precision checks and optimizer analyses, addressing important gaps in v1's comparisons. Broader PDE and inverse-problem tests also strengthen applicability evidence. Some new experiments remain incompletely specified, and Appendix E.6's Burgers Adam error conflicts with Table 10, but these reporting defects do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support.
